# A Heartwarming Tech Project: Crafting a Music Controller for Kids

In a world where technology often feels distant and complex, one father has taken a refreshing approach to blend coding and parenting. Jeff McCune, a developer and father, recently shared his journey of creating a simple music controller for his five-year-old son, designed to control a Sonos Play:1 speaker using an M5Stack CardPuter v1.1 device powered by an ESP32-S3 chip. The project, aptly named **sonoserve**, is not just a technical endeavor, but a delightful way to foster his son’s love for music.

## The Inspiration Behind sonoserve

The idea sprouted from a desire to give his child an interactive way to engage with music. As any parent knows, children often have their favorite songs or playlists that they want to repeat endlessly. Jeff envisioned a tool that would allow his son to easily restart his favorite tunes, empowering him to explore music independently. The project took approximately a day to develop, with the backend built using Go, while the controller utilized C++.

In his post on Hacker News, Jeff expressed the joy of focusing on his son's experience rather than getting bogged down in the intricacies of coding. He relied on a coding agent to handle much of the programming, allowing him to enjoy the process of creation with his child. 

## A Peek Inside the Code

The repository for sonoserve on GitHub showcases a well-structured project with a variety of files, including `.gitignore`, README documentation, and scripts for deployment and development. Key programming languages used in the project include Go (62.9%), C++ (17.2%), and TypeScript (8.9%), highlighting a blend of modern coding practices and utilities.

The accompanying user stories resonate with parents everywhere:

- As a kid, I’d like to restart my favorite playlist so that I can listen to my favorite music.
- As a kid, I’d like to play my favorite tracks.

These simple yet profound statements reflect the heart of the project: creating a joyful and engaging music experience for children.

# Monorail: Transforming CSS Animations into Interactive Graphs

In the ever-evolving landscape of web development, tools that enhance interactivity and visualization are invaluable. Enter **Monorail**, a new library designed to convert CSS keyframe animations into interactive SVG graphs. This innovative approach not only provides developers with a way to visualize animations but also opens the door to a myriad of creative possibilities.

## The Inspiration Behind Monorail

The creator of Monorail initially sought to produce a few simple graphs for a blog post. Instead of opting for the straightforward route of piecing together static SVG images, they embarked on an ambitious journey to develop a library that could dynamically interpret CSS animations. What began as a modest project quickly morphed into a comprehensive tool, complete with its own set of challenges and intricacies. The result? A library that not only meets the creator's needs but also serves as a resource for other developers looking to enhance their projects.

The library is open-source, licensed under MIT, and is built with TypeScript, ensuring it remains lightweight with no external dependencies. Interested developers can find the source code on [GitHub](https://github.com/Stanko/monorail), along with documentation on how to integrate it into their own projects.

## Features and Functionality

Monorail's core function is to parse CSS keyframe animations and translate them into interactive graphs. This unique capability allows users to visualize the timing and flow of animations in a way that static images simply cannot achieve. The library includes an example for users to experiment with, showcasing the potential of the tool in real-time.

### A Community Conversation

The launch of Monorail sparked a lively discussion among developers on Hacker News. Users were quick to express their enthusiasm for the library, with one commenter reflecting on the interesting challenge of flattening colors into a single-dimensional value for the graphs. Questions arose regarding the color conversion process, revealing a thoughtful exchange about the intricacies of CSS and color theory.

The creator responded, noting that while the initial approach involved a straightforward multiplication of RGB values, there is room for improvement. Suggestions to explore different color spaces, like HSL or OKLch, were welcomed, indicating a commitment to refining the tool based on community feedback.

Additionally, a few developers shared their aspirations for the library. One user proposed the idea of making the chart values draggable, allowing for real-time updates to the CSS animation—a concept that could elevate the interactivity of Monorail even further.

## A New Frontier for Developers

Monorail is more than just a tool; it represents a shift in how web developers can approach animation and visualization. By transforming CSS keyframe animations into interactive graphs, it opens avenues for deeper engagement with content and design. Whether you’re a seasoned developer or a newcomer looking to enhance your skills, Monorail offers an exciting opportunity to explore the intersection of animation and data visualization.

# Measuring Power Network Frequency Using Everyday Items

In an era where electricity is the lifeblood of modern infrastructure, monitoring power networks has become increasingly critical. Recently, a fascinating story emerged from the Baltic states, where the electricity grid is undergoing a significant transition: moving from synchronization with the Russian electric grid to alignment with the continental European electrical grid. This transition, which began on February 8, 2025, involves a series of complex steps, including disconnecting from the Russian grid, operating as an isolated system, and ultimately synchronizing with the EU network.

As this transformation unfolds, one curious individual sought to monitor the frequency changes occurring during this pivotal moment. Lacking the specialized equipment typically used for such measurements and mindful of the dangers associated with mains voltage, they turned to an inventive solution: repurposing an audio cable as an antenna. By wrapping it around a power cable and connecting it to a computer’s audio input, they aimed to detect the frequency changes.

### The DIY Frequency Measurement Setup

Initial attempts to record audio signals resulted in a flat line on the screen. However, with some adjustments and normalization, a noisy sine wave around 50Hz emerged. This discovery sparked a creative endeavor to develop a Python script capable of analyzing the frequency using basic Digital Signal Processing (DSP) techniques. The script employs a Hann windowed Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) to dissect the audio data, extract frequency components, and identify peak frequencies through quadratic interpolation. Despite the challenges posed by a low sample rate, the author was determined to refine their method.

### Comparing DIY Data with Professional Sources

To validate their findings, the author compared their DIY measurements with data from Sympower, which provides an API for retrieving power network frequency information. Remarkably, the DIY setup produced surprisingly accurate results, measuring the correct frequency with only minor time lag and output smoothing. The author set up a logger to continuously collect data, eager to observe the precise moment when the transition to the European network occurred.

In an update, the author shared a link to an API for the European network frequency, allowing them to plot their measurements alongside the official data. The synchronizing event between the two networks was clearly visible in the results, marking a successful intersection of amateur ingenuity and critical infrastructure monitoring.

# Revolutionizing Coding Management: Meet Vibe Kanban

In the ever-evolving landscape of software development, tools that enhance productivity are invaluable. Enter **Vibe Kanban**, a platform designed to streamline the management of AI coding agents through a Kanban board interface. Developed by Louis and his team, Vibe Kanban emerged from a common frustration: the inefficiencies of waiting for AI agents to complete tasks while engineers find themselves distracted. 

### The Vision Behind Vibe Kanban

Louis shared that the inspiration for Vibe Kanban stemmed from the time wasted during the 2-5 minutes it often takes coding agents to process tasks. Instead of simply waiting, why not allow coding agents to work in the background while human engineers focus on planning future work or reviewing completed tasks? This innovative approach not only boosts productivity but also ensures that time spent waiting translates into meaningful work.

The platform allows users to effortlessly manage multiple coding agents, orchestrating their execution while keeping track of task statuses. Vibe Kanban centralizes the configuration of coding agent settings and enables the review of their outputs—all within an intuitive Kanban board structure.

### Features That Enhance Workflow

Vibe Kanban comes packed with features aimed at simplifying the development process:

- **Multiple Agent Management**: Effortlessly switch between different coding agents to maximize workflow.
- **Task Tracking**: Easily view the status of coding agents and their tasks.
- **Centralized Configuration**: Manage the settings of coding agents from one location.
- **Development Server**: Run a development server to test and review outputs seamlessly.

Installation is straightforward: authenticate with a coding agent and run the command `npx vibe-kanban`. For those interested in development, ensure you have the latest versions of Rust, Node.js, and pnpm.

### Community Feedback and Iteration

Following the open-source release of Vibe Kanban, feedback has been overwhelmingly positive. Users have lauded its potential to significantly increase productivity, with some comparing the experience to previous leaps in efficiency when they first adopted AI tools like Cursor. However, feedback isn't always glowing; concerns have been raised regarding user privacy and data handling practices.

One user pointed out that the platform’s default analytics settings could collect identifiable information such as email addresses and GitHub usernames. In response, the Vibe Kanban team quickly addressed these concerns with a pull request to implement an opt-in feature for analytics. Such responsiveness to user feedback reflects a commitment to maintaining trust and transparency.

### Bridging the Gap Between AI and Human Collaboration

As AI coding agents become increasingly prevalent in software development, Vibe Kanban positions itself as a vital tool for engineers. It provides a framework for orchestrating the complex interplay between coding agents and human oversight, allowing developers to focus on higher-level tasks. # Exploring OpenFront: A New Frontier in Multiplayer Strategy Gaming

In the vibrant digital landscape of multiplayer gaming, a new contender has emerged: **OpenFront**. This browser-based game invites players into a realm of strategic decision-making, where the management of resources and territorial expansion is key to survival and dominance. With its latest update introducing trains and factories, the game is set to enhance the complexity and enjoyment for avid strategists.

## Gameplay Mechanics and Strategies

OpenFront is primarily focused on managing compounding growth while navigating discrete losses. The logistics of growth are essential, as players must balance their population cap with strategic military actions. A fascinating strategy shared by players involves **trademaxxing**, which focuses on building a network of ports to generate wealth. By forming alliances and carefully managing troop deployment, players can thrive in an environment filled with potential threats.

One player shared their approach: "The fastest way to make money is to get lots of ports and ally with people near and far. Boats give you more gold depending on their distance traveled." This strategy highlights how crucial economic alliances are in the game, allowing players to focus on building a robust military without overextending themselves.

## Community Insights and Development

OpenFront is open-source, inviting contributions from developers and players alike. As one user noted, "It is heavily inspired by territorial.io," a simpler game that has garnered its own fan base. The development of OpenFront stems from a fork of **warfront.io**, which lacked multiplayer features. With a dedicated team of contributors, OpenFront has evolved significantly, yet players have noted areas for improvement, particularly in its user interface and endgame mechanics.

Despite the developer's commitment to making OpenFront a collaborative project, concerns about commercialization have surfaced. One user pointed out that a for-profit company is involved in the operations, raising questions about the future direction of the game. However, the creator clarified, "I created an LLC mostly for tax purposes, but I maintain 100% ownership." This transparency has been welcomed by the community, who appreciate the developer's dedication to the game's integrity.

## Learning Curve and Player Experiences

As with many strategy games, newcomers may find OpenFront initially challenging. Players have shared their experiences navigating the game's mechanics, with one noting, "You must plant your nation during the generation phase, otherwise you won't exist in the game!!!" This insight reflects the learning curve many experience, prompting suggestions for more intuitive tutorials and guides.

For those looking to sharpen their skills, community members have recommended watching gameplay videos. "I discovered this game through Ultimus Rex's YouTube channel," one player remarked, emphasizing the value of learning from experienced players. This communal approach to sharing knowledge not only fosters a supportive gaming environment but also enhances the overall experience for both newcomers and veterans.
